thread:
alex: Heads-up — proposing FlashAttention v2/v3 gating plan for the runtime. Goal: pick an attention kernel by (model_size, seq_len, device, KV-mode) and expose a safe feature-flagged rollout path.

maya: +1. Any microbench numbers or surprising regressions yet?

alex: Quick summary from local runs on A100/H100 and our perf lab. TL;DR: v3 is better for long sequences and memory-constrained workloads on H100, but we saw a small regression on short-seq single-stream KV workloads. Details in the table below.

alex: ```
model,seq,batch,device,FA_v2_ms,FA_v3_ms,notes
gpt2,128,1,A100,12.3,13.1, v3 slight overhead on tiny seq
gpt2,1024,1,A100,120.4,98.7, v3 wins for long seq on A100
llama-13b,512,8,H100,60.1,52.3, v3 wins at moderate batch
llama-70b,2048,1,H100,450,420, v3 better mem and perf
kv-heavy,256,1,A100,30.2,38.9, v3 regresses with paged-KV layout
```

alex: Notes: the "kv-heavy" line is when we stress paged-KV path (many cache misses / small writes). FA v3's new memory layout currently causes extra copies in our KV path which increases latency in low-batch single-stream scenarios.

sam: Can you summarize actionable kernel-selection rules?

alex: Draft rules: 
- if device == H100 and seq >= 1024 -> prefer flash_v3
- elif device == A100 and batch <= 2 and seq <= 512 -> prefer flash_v2
- elif workload uses paged-KV with many partial updates -> prefer fused_attention (safer)
- else -> default to flash_v3 for throughput-focused cases

julia: Important callout: our continuous-batching heuristics can hide regressions. If we switch kernels for a particular seq/device pair, cold-start single-stream requests (batch=1) can be hit much harder. We should include per-route fallback and tail-latency monitoring.

kevin: Proposal: gate by feature-flags and region canaries. Metrics via perf-bot: p50/p95/p99, mem-alloc, OOMs, and token-level quality diffs. Rollout plan: dev canary -> 1% prod -> 10% -> 50% with automated rollbacks.

alex: Example config snippet for runtime kernel_preference (proposal):
```yaml
attn:
  kernel_preference:
    - condition: device == H100 and seq >= 1024
      kernel: flash_v3
    - condition: batch <= 2 and seq <= 512 and device == A100
      kernel: flash_v2
    - condition: workload.kv_mode == paged
      kernel: fused_attention
    - kernel: flash_v3
```

maya: We should also expose a soft-weighted selector so we can A/B kernels within a machine (e.g., prefer v3 80% / fallback 20% for stability testing). Something like `kernel_selector_mode: weighted`.

sam: For testing: unit tests for kernel_selector, end-to-end perf harness that simulates continuous batching and KV cache patterns, and an offline eval comparing logprobs over established prompt sets.

alex: I ran a quick profile (nsight & perf) — main hotspots when v3 regressed: extra memcpy in kv-update path and an unexpected cuda-sync in paged attention edge-case. We'll open a follow-up issue to see if we can eliminate the memcpy.

perf-bot: Running perf/regression job: infra/perf/flash-v3-canary (queued). Will post results to #eng-runtime when done. :robot_face:

julia: Rollback triggers suggestion: any sustained >10% regression on p99 latency for a route, >15% increase in memory, or token-level logprob delta >0.8 on guard evals. Also trigger on any OOMs.

kevin: Add observability: per-route kernel split, token-cost accounting, and kv-hit/miss counters emitted to console. We need to ensure RBAC flags so we can flip kernels per-customer for Dedicated/Private environments.

alex: Can we add a small compatibility shim so that v3 can be used without changing on-disk KV layout? If not feasible quickly, we'll keep v3 disabled for paged-KV by default.

maya: I'll own the canary runbook and dashboards (requested). Will add a smoke test matrix: correctness (logprobs), latency (p50/p95/p99), mem, and downstream app traces.

sam: I'll implement the kernel-selection rules + weighted selector and unit tests. I'll also add a perf sim that reproduces the paged-KV memcpy pattern.

alex: Thanks — I'll open the feature-flag PR and wire the rollout policy. We'll coordinate the perf-bot jobs and add alerts.

kevin: Timeline suggestion: PR + bench docs by EOD Fri, dev canary next week, prod canary 1 week after if green.

maya: ack.

julia: I'll draft the rollback playbook and example alert runbook.

sam: thumbs-up.

alex: Great. Tagging follow-ups: alex -> PR + rollout, maya -> canary + dashboards, sam -> selector/tests, julia -> rollback playbook. Perf-bot: please post the perf job results and we'll reconvene on next steps. :white_check_mark:
